newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oerlikon to pay first dividend in decade.
newsitem.headline: Oerlikon to pay first dividend in decade.

text.p: Swiss arms-to-fashion conglomerate Oerlikon Buehrle Holding AG said on Wednesday it would pay its first dividend in a decade after 1996 net profit rebounded to 62 million Swiss francs from three million.
The dividend proposal would be 1.20 Swiss francs per registered share, a company spokeswoman said. That was equivalent to six percent of share capital or 15 million Swiss francs.

Oerlikon last paid a dividend on 1985 results, when it gave out five percent of share capital or 19.2 million francs, then fell into a long period of losses and restructuring at major units led by defence and weapons business Oerlikon-Contraves.
Oerlikon's other divisions are shoes and fashion maker Bally, vacuum and surface technology unit Balzers and Leybold, small aircraft maker Pilatus and real estate division Immobilien.
"The group is recovering from the previous year's setback and is now on track with a concentrated portfolio," Oerlikon said in a statement on 1996 results.

It said 1996 net profit of 62 million Swiss francs marked a return to a growth trend that had started in 1992 but was cut off last year by a plunge to three million Swiss francs from 75 million in 1994 .
This plunge was caused mainly by operating setbacks at Bally and restructuring at Contraves, it said.
Sales in 1996 were down to 3.6 billion Swiss francs from 3.8 billion due to divestments. Operating profit was 204 million after 139 million in 1995.
